transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Time: 11:00 AM PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Solutions), Alex (Netcon CTO), Mei (Platform), Ravi (SecOps), Jordan (ML Eng), Tara (SRE)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on integration approach for Netcon's LLM gateway/proxy, evaluation of Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private, SDK and LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, rate limiting/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer wants clear perf benchmarks and a path to a short pilot that includes VPC options and KMS integration.

Topics Covered:
- Current stack and traffic shape
- Gateway/proxy placement and sidecar vs centralized gateway
- SDKs and connectors (LangChain, LlamaIndex, internal SDKs)
- Rate limits, quotas, and burst policies
- Observability: traces, token-level cost, and audit logs
- Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS/HSM, data residency
- Next steps and pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone thanks for doing this, uh we'll keep it tight 45-60 minutes and then we can follow up with the se deep dive, do folks have any quick intros?
[00:07] Alex: yeah Alex here, CTO at Netcon. We're evaluating options for an LLM gateway that can sit front of our microservices. Main concerns are multi-team quotaing and cost predictability.
[00:18] Sophie: great, and Daniel and Priya are our technical leads on the infra side. Daniel, quick context on what Redwood usually sees for gateway patterns?
[00:27] Daniel: sure, um two common patterns: sidecar per service (low-latency local routing) or centralized gateway/proxy — we see centralized when teams want unified observability and quotaing. There's tradeoffs: sidecar scales with pods, centralized gives single point to enforce rate limits and cache prefix.
[00:45] Mei: can you nuance cache prefix? We use a lot of short prompts for completions and then longer chats. How would that work with KV cache?
[00:53] Daniel: right, so Redwood has automatic prefix and KV caching — or sorry, I keep saying KV cash — it's K-V cache — that preserves context for chat-style flows and reduces tokens downstream. For sidecar, cache is local to the pod, for centralized you can have a shared cache cluster which helps reuse across services.
[01:12] Jordan: do you support Lang Chain and Llama Index connectors out of the box? We have a lot of retrieval-augmented cases.
[01:18] Priya: yes, we have SDKs with first-class LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations; we provide starter templates. There's a small adapter you drop in and you'll get consistent token accounting and streaming. The adapter also supports the Redwood proxy auth flow if you want to use a gateway.
[01:30] Tara: Streaming — we need low tail latency. Hosted api — how does watchdog behave for tail? Any SLA?
[01:36] Sophie: hosted has published latency profiles; dedicated gets you predictable throughput and tighter SLOs. For tail latency sensitive workloads we often recommend dedicated with reserved pools or private deployment if you need on-prem.
[01:48] Alex: okay what about quotas — we have multiple internal teams and external partners, need per-team quotas, burst allowances, and ability to throttle gracefully.
[01:57] Daniel: Redwood's routing layer supports policy-based routing and quotaing — you can set per-token or per-request limits, token budgets per API key, and burst policies. Throttles can return re-try-after headers and we have a built-in graceful degradation policy to fallback to smaller models or cached responses.
[02:15] Ravi: security questions — do you have SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, and KMS support? Also audit logs retention, encryption in transit and at rest?
[02:25] Sophie: yes, SAML SSO and SCIM, RBAC, full audit logs in the console. KMS integrations are supported for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer a managed key option or customer-managed keys in dedicated+private. We'll share the security pack after.
[02:38] Mei: what concerns me is network egress patterns. If we choose hosted, data leaves the VPC, and we need to know how that maps to our compliance. What are the private options?
[02:48] Priya: two options: Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering/private link so traffic stays in cloud region and you control routing, or Redwood Private which is a customer-managed control plane that can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem. Private supports air-gapped installs with HSM/KMS integrations.
[03:06] Alex: latency wise, if we do VPC peering vs dedicated-reserved pool, what's the extra hop?
[03:11] Daniel: typically a few ms of network hop on top of inference. The dominant factor is batch size and model choice. If you're running 2048-token chat on a 4090 variant that we host, you'll see different tail characteristics. We'll need to run a benchmark with your prompt sets to be precise.
[03:27] Jordan: about SDKs, our infra is Go and Python. Do you have native Go SDK? And how's the auth?
[03:34] Priya: Python and Node are first-class; we have a Go SDK in beta. Auth is API key or mTLS for private endpoints; we also support token exchange for short-lived credentials.
[03:44] Jordan: nice. For LangChain, do you handle agent tooling / function calling?
[03:48] Daniel: yes, function/tool-calling and structured output are supported. The LangChain adapter translates function call semantics and you get streaming structured responses.
[03:56] Mei: observability — we need tracing tied to our trace ids. Can we inject our trace context and get per-token cost breakdown?
[04:03] Sophie: console supports token-level cost and latency breakdowns and you can pass tracing headers — we capture trace ids and expose per-request metrics. We also have tracing hooks for Jaeger/Zipkin and can push spans into your observability pipeline.
[04:15] Tara: what about error rates during model fallback? If a model goes OOM do you automatically fall back and how will that show up in metrics?
[04:22] Daniel: there are automatic fallback policies: model variant fallback and regional fallback; failures are surfaced as events and you'll see retried requests and fallback flags in the trace and cost breakdown.
[04:32] Alex: licensing and pricing — curious about commitment levels. Also want dedicated pool sizing guidance.
[04:38] Sophie: we'll send a committed capacity proposal; Dedicated is subscription + usage for burst. We'll include recommended GPU pool sizes based on your RPS and latency target after we see your request distribution.
[04:49] Ravi: for procurement we'll need SOC2, ISO docs and an audit page.
[04:53] Sophie: absolutely, we'll upload SOC2, ISO, and our security questionnaire link in the shared drive.
[04:58] Mei: small technical nit — do you support prefix caching when using LangChain retrieval? We want to cache parts of the retrieval pipeline to reduce tokens.
[05:06] Daniel: yes, you can cache embeddings and intermediate prompts at the gateway level; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching settings for your workload.
[05:15] Jordan: for the pilot can we get a sandbox tenant and sample LangChain demo so our ML folks can iterate rapidly?
[05:20] Priya: yes we'll provision a trial tenant and a sample repo with LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors. We'll include sample workload for RAG and streaming.
[05:27] Alex: timelines — we'd like a pilot in early December, run for 2 weeks, then decide by end of year.
[05:33] Sophie: sounds doable, we propose the benchmark deep-dive on 2026-12-08, and provisioning the trial by 2026-12-06.
[05:40] Tara: any blockers from your side for peering? We have networking constraints but can open a few CIDR ranges.
[05:46] Priya: we'll coordinate with your infra team, Mei, on exact peering and firewall rules.
[05:50] Mei: OK I'll share the traffic shape and current RPS histogram.
[05:53] Sophie: cool, quick recap — we'll send pricing and security docs, Daniel will prepare a benchmark plan and SDK examples, and Priya will provision a trial tenant and example LangChain/LlamaIndex repo. Next call: SE perf deep-dive 12/08. Any other questions?
[06:08] Alex: none from me, appreciate it.
[06:10] Ravi: thanks all.
[06:12] Sophie: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and action items.

End of transcript.
